summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with abdominal pain, shortness of breath, chest pain, fever, and new-onset atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. He had recently been discharged after treatment for pneumonia, C. difficile infection, and cellulitis. Evaluation revealed no pulmonary embolism or ischemic heart disease. His symptoms were attributed to atrial fibrillation likely triggered by dehydration, pain, and recent chemotherapy. Constipation contributed to abdominal pain, which resolved with bowel movement. He was treated with intravenous diltiazem, transitioned to oral diltiazem, and broad-spectrum antibiotics were discontinued after negative cultures. A PICC line was placed for reliable venous access. He improved clinically, with resolution of symptoms and stabilization of lab values, and was discharged home with plans for cardiology follow-up and continuation of oral vancomycin and chemotherapy prophylaxis.
